recto: Average speed of sound in soft tissue (m/s and mm/µs)? What sets it?
verso: 1540 m/s = 1.54 mm/µs. Set by the medium only (stiffness, density), never by frequency.
T = 1/f ; λ = c/f (5 MHz in soft tissue: T = 0.2 µs, λ ≈ 0.31 mm)

recto: What do +3 dB and +10 dB mean for intensity?
verso: +3 dB: intensity doubled ; −3 dB: halved ; +10 dB: ×10

recto: Pulse duration and spatial pulse length?
verso: PD = n × T = n/f ; SPL = n × λ (n = cycles per pulse)

recto: Pulse repetition period in soft tissue, rule of thumb?
verso: About 13 µs per cm of imaging depth (PRP = 2d/c). Deeper: PRP up, PRF down, duty factor down.

recto: Duty factor: formula and CW value?
verso: DF = PD/PRP ; 100% for continuous wave, very small for imaging.

recto: Highest and lowest intensities? Which one relates to heating?
verso: Highest SPTP, lowest SATA. SPTA relates to tissue heating.
≈ 0.5 dB/cm/MHz ; pulse–echo path = 2 × depth (5 MHz at 6 cm depth: 30 dB).

recto: Intensity reflection coefficient at normal incidence?
verso: IRC = ((Z₂ − Z₁)/(Z₂ + Z₁))² ; ITC = 1 − IRC ; Z = ρc. Equal impedances: no echo.
Oblique incidence AND different propagation speeds (Snell: sin θt / sin θi = c₂/c₁).

recto: Axial resolution formula and how to improve it?
verso: Axial = SPL/2 = nλ/2. Higher frequency, fewer cycles (more backing). Smaller number = better.

recto: Lateral resolution equals…? Where is it best?
verso: Beam width ; best at the focus.
Greater depth, more lines per frame, more focal zones (FR = c / (2 d N F)).
λ/4 ; impedance between element and skin to improve transmission.
Shorter pulse, better axial resolution, wider bandwidth, lower Q factor, lower sensitivity.

recto: Near zone length formula? Effect of doubling diameter?
verso: NZL = D²/(4λ) = D²f/(4c) ; diameter ×2 gives NZL ×4.
Δf = 2 f₀ v cos θ / c ; no shift at 90° (cos 90° = 0).

recto: Nyquist limit? When does aliasing occur?
verso: Nyquist = PRF/2 ; aliasing when the Doppler shift exceeds PRF/2 (pulsed wave only).
Raise scale (PRF), move baseline, lower f₀, shallower sample gate, switch to CW.
Power: amplitude only, no direction, no aliasing, more sensitive to slow flow. Color: mean velocity and direction, can alias.
ΔP ≈ 4v² (mmHg, v in m/s): 3 m/s gives 36 mmHg.

recto: Mirror image artifact: where is the copy?
verso: Deeper than the true structure, behind a strong specular reflector (e.g. diaphragm).
Shadowing: high attenuation (stone, bone, gas). Enhancement: low attenuation (fluid).

recto: Speed error: medium slower than 1540 m/s?
verso: Reflector displayed too deep (and too shallow if the medium is faster).
MI = p_r / √f (derated peak rarefactional pressure in MPa, f in MHz).
Lowest output and shortest time giving a diagnostic image; raise gain before output power; monitor TI and MI.
Sensitivity = TP/(TP + FN) ; specificity = TN/(TN + FP).
